test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Two trains are running on parallel tracks towards each other. Train A is 250 meters long and is moving at a speed of 90 km/h. Train B is 150 meters long and is moving at a speed of 60 km/h. How much time (rounded off to the nearest seconds) will it take for Train A to completely pass Train B?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Opposite direction ⇒ add speeds

Total distance = 250 + 150 = 400 m

Relative speed = 90 + 60 = 150 km/h = 41.67 m/s

Time = 400 ÷ 41.67 ≈ 9.6 sec

**∴ Answer = 10 seconds**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of A = 250 m, Length of B = 150 m

Speed of A = 90 km/h, Speed of B = 60 km/h

**Formula used:**

Time = Total distance ÷ Relative speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total distance = 250 + 150 = 400 m

⇒ Relative speed = 90 + 60 = 150 km/h

⇒ Convert speed = 150 × (5/18) = 41.67 m/s

⇒ Time = 400 ÷ 41.67 ≈ 9.6 sec

⇒ Rounded off = 10 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 10 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

Opposite direction ⇒ speeds are added

Unit Conversion

km/h to m/s ⇒ multiply by 5/18

Train Rule

Total distance = sum of lengths
